items.headline: Germany: Is it possible to replace the chancellor?
items.snippet: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's record-low approval ratings have emboldened his opponents. There are three ways to remove a chancellor from office in Germany.

items.snippet: Germany's far-right AfD party is riding high after its latest electoral triumph in Saxony-Anhalt. But one question remains: Does it actually want to govern?

items.headline: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
items.snippet: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

items.headline: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
items.snippet: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

items.snippet: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

items.headline: Organized crime and drug-related deaths rise Germany
items.snippet: In the annual report on organized crime, German police say cocaine is a danger for the state and society and cases of money laundering have increased.

items.headline: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
items.snippet: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

items.headline: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
items.snippet: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

items.headline: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
items.snippet: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

items.headline: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
items.snippet: German judges and prosecutors warn that the coalition needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

items.headline: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
items.snippet: The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

items.headline: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
items.snippet: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

items.headline: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
items.snippet: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

items.headline: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
items.snippet: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

items.headline: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
items.snippet: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

items.headline: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
items.snippet: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

items.headline: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
items.snippet: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

items.headline: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
items.snippet: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

items.headline: UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
items.snippet: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

items.headline: Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
items.snippet: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

items.headline: Chancellor Merz seeks CDU support amid far-right AfD surge
items.snippet: Following the CDU's crushing defeat in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, many are expressing doubts about the party's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz. But the CDU doesn't appear to have a viable alternative.

items.headline: Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
items.snippet: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

items.headline: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
items.snippet: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

items.headline: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
items.snippet: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

items.headline: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
items.snippet: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

items.headline: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
items.snippet: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

items.headline: Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
items.snippet: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

items.headline: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
items.snippet: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

items.headline: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
items.snippet: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

items.headline: Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
